English.rule: A basic English sentence normally needs a subject and a verb.
English.use: Statements and simple ideas.
mistakes: ❌ Work every day. → ✅ I work every day.
❌ She happy. → ✅ She is happy.

English.rule: Use forms of be for identity, description, age, location and states.
English.use: Identity, description, location and temporary states.
English.formation: I am; you/we/they are; he/she/it is.
mistakes: ❌ She are tired. → ✅ She is tired.
❌ I is ready. → ✅ I am ready.

English.rule: Use the base verb for I/you/we/they and add -s or -es for he/she/it.
English.use: Habits, routines, repeated actions and facts.
English.formation: I work; she works; do/does for questions and negatives.
mistakes: ❌ She work here. → ✅ She works here.
❌ Does she works? → ✅ Does she work?

English.rule: Use am/is/are + -ing for an action happening now or around now.
English.use: Actions in progress and temporary situations.
mistakes: ❌ I studying. → ✅ I am studying.
❌ She is cook. → ✅ She is cooking.

English.rule: Use there is for singular and there are for plural existence.
English.use: Saying that something exists or is present.
English.formation: There is + singular; There are + plural.
English.hook: THERE IS ONE • THERE ARE MANY
examples: There are two books on the table.
mistakes: ❌ There is two books. → ✅ There are two books.

English.rule: Use a/an for one non-specific countable noun and the for a specific or known noun.
English.use: Introducing and identifying nouns.
English.formation: a before consonant sound; an before vowel sound; the for specific reference.
English.hook: A/AN = ONE OF MANY • THE = KNOWN
examples: I saw a dog. The dog was friendly.
mistakes: ❌ an university → ✅ a university (consonant sound /juː/)

English.rule: Countable nouns have singular/plural forms; many substances and abstract nouns are uncountable.
English.use: Choosing articles, plurals and quantity words.
English.hook: COUNT IT? → A BOOK • CAN'T COUNT IT → WATER
mistakes: ❌ advices → ✅ advice / pieces of advice
❌ informations → ✅ information

English.rule: Pronouns replace nouns and change form according to their grammatical role.
English.use: Avoiding repetition and marking subject/object/possessive roles.
English.hook: WHO DOES IT? → SUBJECT • WHO RECEIVES IT? → OBJECT
mistakes: ❌ Me went home. → ✅ I went home.

English.rule: Use possessive determiners before nouns and possessive pronouns without a following noun.
English.use: Showing ownership or relationship.
English.hook: MY BOOK • THE BOOK IS MINE
mistakes: ❌ This is mine car. → ✅ This is my car.

English.rule: Use do/does to form present-simple questions with ordinary verbs.
English.use: Asking about habits, facts and routines.
English.formation: Do + I/you/we/they + verb? Does + he/she/it + verb?
mistakes: ❌ Does she likes tea? → ✅ Does she like tea?

English.rule: Who, what, where, when, why and how ask for different information.
English.use: Building useful everyday questions.
English.hook: WHO • WHAT • WHERE • WHEN • WHY • HOW
mistakes: ❌ Where you live? → ✅ Where do you live?

English.rule: Use not with be and do/does/did not with ordinary verbs.
English.use: Saying something is not true or does not happen.
English.formation: be + not; do/does/did + not + base verb.
mistakes: ❌ She doesn't goes. → ✅ She doesn't go.

English.rule: Common place prepositions include in, on, at, under, behind, between and next to.
English.use: Describing where people and things are.
examples: The keys are on the table.
The car is in the garage.
mistakes: ❌ on the room → ✅ in the room

English.rule: Use at for clock times, on for days/dates and in for months/years/longer periods.
English.use: Talking about when something happens.
English.formation: at 5; on Monday; in July; in 2026.
English.hook: AT TIME • ON DAY • IN PERIOD
mistakes: ❌ in Monday → ✅ on Monday

English.rule: Use the past form for completed actions at a finished past time.
English.use: Finished events and sequences in the past.
English.formation: regular -ed; irregular past forms; did for questions/negatives.
mistakes: ❌ Did you went? → ✅ Did you go?

English.rule: Use was/were + -ing for an action in progress at a past time.
English.use: Background actions and interrupted events.
examples: I was sleeping when you called.
mistakes: ❌ I was sleep. → ✅ I was sleeping.

English.rule: Use have/has + past participle for past actions connected to the present.
English.use: Experience, recent results and unfinished time periods.
English.hook: HAVE/HAS + V3 → PAST CONNECTED TO NOW
mistakes: ❌ She have finished. → ✅ She has finished.

English.rule: Present perfect connects past to now; past simple places a completed event in finished past time.
English.use: Choosing between experience/current relevance and finished-time events.
English.hook: FINISHED TIME → PAST • NO FINISHED TIME → OFTEN PERFECT
mistakes: ❌ I have visited Paris in 2022. → Prefer: I visited Paris in 2022.

English.rule: Use will + base verb for predictions, decisions made now, promises and offers.
English.use: Future predictions, spontaneous decisions and promises.
mistakes: ❌ I will to go. → ✅ I will go.

English.rule: Use be going to + base verb for plans and predictions based on present evidence.
English.use: Intentions and visible evidence.
examples: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
mistakes: ❌ I going to study. → ✅ I am going to study.

English.rule: Can, could, may, might, must and should are followed by the base verb.
English.use: Ability, possibility, obligation, advice and permission.
mistakes: ❌ He can swims. → ✅ He can swim.

English.rule: Use comparative forms to compare two things and superlatives for the highest degree in a group.
English.use: Comparing people, places and things.
mistakes: ❌ more faster → ✅ faster

English.rule: Zero conditional describes general truths; first conditional describes real future possibilities.
English.use: Facts, rules, warnings and possible future results.
English.formation: If + present, present; If + present, will + base.
examples: If you heat ice, it melts.
If it rains, I will stay home.
mistakes: ❌ If it will rain, I will stay home. → ✅ If it rains, I will stay home.

English.rule: Use if + past, would + base for unreal or unlikely present/future situations.
English.use: Imaginary situations and advice.
examples: If I had more time, I would travel.
If I were you, I'd wait.
mistakes: ❌ If I would have time... → ✅ If I had time...
questions: If I were rich, I ___ travel.

English.rule: Use be + past participle when the action is more important than the doer.
English.use: Processes, reports and formal writing.
English.formation: be + V3, with tense carried by be.
examples: The report will be published tomorrow.
mistakes: ❌ The report published. → ✅ The report was published.

English.rule: Use who for people, which for things, that for people/things in defining clauses, and whose for possession.
English.use: Adding information about a noun.
examples: The woman who called is my sister.
This is the book that I bought.
mistakes: ❌ The man which called → ✅ The man who called
questions: The book ___ I bought is here.

English.rule: Reported speech tells what someone said without quoting the exact words.
English.use: Reporting statements and questions.
English.formation: said/told + reported clause; tense often shifts back.
examples: She said, “I am tired.” → She said that she was tired.
He told me he was busy.
mistakes: ❌ He said me... → ✅ He told me... / He said...

English.rule: Some verbs are followed by -ing and others by to + base; meaning can sometimes change.
English.use: Talking about activities, plans and verb complements.
English.formation: enjoy + -ing; want + to + verb; decide + to + verb.
mistakes: ❌ I enjoy to read. → ✅ I enjoy reading.

English.rule: Conjunctions connect ideas and show contrast, reason, time, condition or result.
English.use: Making longer, clearer sentences.
English.formation: because, although, while, when, if, so, therefore.
English.hook: CONNECT IDEAS, DON'T JUST ADD SENTENCES
examples: I stayed home because it rained.
Although he was tired, he worked.
mistakes: ❌ Although he was tired but he worked. → Remove but.

English.rule: Third conditional describes unreal past results; mixed conditionals connect past conditions with present results.
English.use: Regret, hypothetical past and present consequences.
English.formation: If + had + V3, would have + V3; mixed forms vary by meaning.
examples: If I had studied, I would have passed.
If I had taken that job, I would live abroad now.
mistakes: ❌ If I would have studied... → ✅ If I had studied...
questions: If she had left earlier, she ___ caught the train.

English.rule: Advanced English uses auxiliary substitution, inversion and emphasis to make writing precise or formal.
English.use: Formal writing and sophisticated expression.
English.formation: Neither do I; Not only..., but...; Rarely do we...
examples: Rarely do we see such results.
Not only did he win, but he also set a record.
mistakes: ❌ Rarely we see... → Formal: Rarely do we see...

Spanish.rule: Spanish commonly uses subject + verb + complement, but subject pronouns are often omitted because the verb shows person.
Spanish.formation: Sujeto + verbo + complemento; pronombre opcional.
mistakes: ❌ Yo trabaja. → ✅ Yo trabajo.

Spanish.rule: Ser expresses identity, origin, profession, characteristics and other relatively essential descriptions.
Spanish.formation: soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son.
mistakes: ❌ Estoy profesor. → ✅ Soy profesor.

Spanish.rule: Estar expresses location, temporary state and conditions.
Spanish.formation: estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están.
mistakes: ❌ Madrid es en España. → ✅ Madrid está en España.

Spanish.rule: Regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs change endings according to the subject.
Spanish.formation: hablar: hablo/hablas/habla; comer: como/comés; vivir: vivo/vives/vive.
mistakes: ❌ Yo hablan. → ✅ Yo hablo.

Spanish.rule: Nouns have grammatical gender; articles agree with noun gender and number.
Spanish.formation: el/la/los/las; un/una/unos/unas.
mistakes: ❌ el casa → ✅ la casa

Spanish.rule: Most nouns form plural with -s after a vowel and -es after a consonant.
Spanish.use: Talking about more than one noun.
Spanish.formation: casa → casas; papel → papeles.
mistakes: ❌ papels → ✅ papeles

Spanish.rule: Spanish subject pronouns may be omitted; object pronouns identify the receiver of an action.
Spanish.formation: yo/me; tú/te; él/lo; ella/la; nosotros/nos; ellos/los/las.
mistakes: ❌ Yo veo él. → Often: Yo lo veo.

Spanish.rule: Possessive adjectives agree with the thing possessed, not with the owner.
Spanish.formation: mi/mis, tu/tus, su/sus, nuestro/a/os/as.
mistakes: ❌ nuestro casa → ✅ nuestra casa

Spanish.rule: Questions can use rising intonation, question words and inverted punctuation.
Spanish.formation: ¿qué?, ¿quién?, ¿dónde?, ¿cuándo?, ¿por qué?, ¿cómo?
mistakes: ❌ Donde vives? → Written Spanish: ¿Dónde vives?

Spanish.rule: Place no before the conjugated verb for basic negation.
Spanish.formation: no + verb; double negatives are grammatical in Spanish.
mistakes: ❌ No no tengo → Avoid unnecessary duplication.

Spanish.rule: Hay means there is/there are and is used for existence.
Spanish.formation: hay + noun; same form for singular and plural.
mistakes: ❌ Hay están tres libros → use hay directly.

Spanish.rule: Common prepositions include a, en, de, con, para and por.
Spanish.use: Location, destination, origin, company and purpose.
Spanish.formation: a = to; en = in/on; de = of/from; para = purpose; por = reason/through.
Spanish.hook: A → TO • EN → IN • DE → FROM
mistakes: ❌ Voy en Madrid. → Destination normally: Voy a Madrid.

Spanish.rule: Use personal a before a specific person as a direct object.
Spanish.use: Talking about people who receive an action.
Spanish.formation: ver a María; conocer a Juan.
mistakes: ❌ Veo María. → ✅ Veo a María.

Spanish.rule: The preterite describes completed past events.
Spanish.formation: hablé, hablaste, habló; fui, fue for ir/ser.
mistakes: ❌ Ayer iba al mercado, when a single completed trip is meant.

Spanish.rule: The imperfect describes habitual, ongoing or background past situations.
Spanish.formation: hablaba, comía, vivía; era, iba, veía.
mistakes: ❌ Cuando era niño, jugué mucho. → Habit: jugaba.

Spanish.rule: Use preterite for the event and imperfect for background or repeated context.
Spanish.formation: event = preterite; background = imperfect.
mistakes: ❌ Use of one tense for every past verb can obscure the story.

Spanish.rule: Estar + gerund describes an action in progress.
Spanish.formation: estoy/estás/está + hablando/comiendo/viviendo.
mistakes: ❌ Estoy estudio. → ✅ Estoy estudiando.

Spanish.rule: Ir a + infinitive expresses a planned or imminent future.
Spanish.formation: voy/vas/va/vamos/vais/van + a + infinitive.
mistakes: ❌ Voy estudiar → ✅ Voy a estudiar.

Spanish.rule: Add future endings to the infinitive; many irregular stems exist.
Spanish.formation: infinitive + é, ás, á, emos, éis, án.
mistakes: ❌ Yo estudiaréé → only one future ending.

Spanish.rule: The conditional expresses hypothetical results, polite requests and possibilities.
Spanish.use: Would, could-like meanings and polite language.
Spanish.formation: infinitive + ía, ías, ía, íamos, íais, ían.
mistakes: ❌ Si tendría tiempo... → In conditional clauses use imperfect subjunctive: Si tuviera...

Spanish.rule: Spanish commands change according to positive/negative form and person.
Spanish.formation: tú positive: habla; negative: no hables; formal forms use subjunctive.
mistakes: ❌ No habla → negative command needs subjunctive: no hables.

Spanish.rule: Haber + past participle expresses a completed action connected to the present.
Spanish.use: Recent events and experiences, especially with present relevance.
Spanish.formation: he/has/ha/hemos/habéis/han + V3.
mistakes: ❌ He comido ayer → with a finished past marker, preterite is often expected: comí ayer.

Spanish.rule: Object pronouns can precede conjugated verbs and attach to infinitives/gerunds/positive commands.
Spanish.formation: me, te, lo/la, le, nos, os, los/las; combinations vary.
mistakes: ❌ Le lo doy → combined indirect + direct becomes se lo.

Spanish.rule: Para commonly expresses purpose, destination or deadline; por commonly expresses cause, exchange, duration, movement through and other relations.
Spanish.formation: para + purpose/destination; por + reason/exchange/duration.
mistakes: ❌ Estudio por aprender → purpose: para aprender.

Spanish.rule: The present subjunctive commonly appears after wishes, recommendations, emotion, doubt and certain conjunctions.
Spanish.formation: que + subjunctive after trigger; regular endings differ from indicative.
mistakes: ❌ Quiero que vienes → trigger requires subjunctive: vengas.

Spanish.rule: Que is the common relative pronoun; quien(es), donde and lo que add more specific meanings.
Spanish.use: Connecting information about nouns and ideas.
Spanish.formation: noun + que + clause; quien for people in suitable contexts.
Spanish.hook: QUE CONNECTS THE NOUN TO ITS CLAUSE
examples: La mujer que vive aquí es mi amiga.
El lugar donde nací es pequeño.
mistakes: ❌ La mujer que ella vive... → avoid unnecessary repeated subject when relative pronoun already fills the role.

Spanish.rule: Spanish often uses se or passive structures to express general or passive meanings without emphasizing the agent.
Spanish.formation: se + verb + noun; ser + participle in formal passive.
mistakes: ❌ Se vende casas → plural agreement: Se venden casas.

Spanish.rule: Reported speech integrates what someone said into a new clause and adjusts references and sometimes tense.
Spanish.formation: dijo que + clause; preguntó si/qué...
Spanish.hook: SAY IT AGAIN, ADJUST THE VIEWPOINT
mistakes: ❌ Dijo me → dijo que / me dijo.

Spanish.rule: The imperfect subjunctive is used for hypothetical, past-dependent or formal subjunctive contexts.
Spanish.use: Unreal conditions, reported wishes and past triggers.
Spanish.formation: -ra/-se forms; e.g. hablara, tuviera, fuera.
mistakes: ❌ Si tendría tiempo → Si tuviera tiempo.

Spanish.rule: Spanish uses different combinations of indicative, subjunctive and conditional to express real, hypothetical and impossible situations.
Spanish.formation: Si + present → future; si + imperfect subjunctive → conditional; si + pluperfect subjunctive → conditional perfect.
mistakes: ❌ Si habría sabido... → Si hubiera sabido...

Spanish.rule: Haya + past participle expresses completed action within a subjunctive context.
Spanish.use: Emotion, doubt or evaluation about a completed action.
Spanish.formation: haya/hayas/haya/hayamos/hayan + V3.
mistakes: ❌ Me alegra que has venido → subjunctive after emotion.

Spanish.rule: Connectors such as aunque, sin embargo, mientras que, a pesar de que and por lo tanto express precise logical relationships.
Spanish.formation: connector + clause; choose indicative/subjunctive according to meaning.
mistakes: ❌ Using every connector as interchangeable can change the logic.

French.rule: French commonly uses subject + verb + complement.
French.formation: Sujet + verbe + complément.
mistakes: ❌ Elle heureux. → ✅ Elle est heureuse.

French.rule: Être expresses identity, description, origin, profession, location in certain constructions and states.
French.formation: je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont.
mistakes: ❌ Je es → ✅ Je suis

French.rule: Avoir means to have and forms many compound tenses.
French.formation: j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont.
mistakes: ❌ Je suis vingt ans → French uses avoir for age: J'ai vingt ans.

French.rule: Regular -er, -ir and some -re verbs use predictable present endings.
French.formation: parler: parle/parles/parle/parlons/parlez/parlent.
mistakes: ❌ Je parles → ✅ Je parle

French.rule: Definite articles agree in gender and number.
French.use: Talking about known or general nouns.
French.formation: le masculine singular; la feminine singular; les plural.
mistakes: ❌ le maison → ✅ la maison

French.rule: Indefinite articles introduce non-specific singular or plural nouns.
French.formation: un masculine; une feminine; des plural.
mistakes: ❌ une livre when livre means book → un livre.

French.rule: Adjectives generally agree with the noun in gender and number.
French.formation: masculine/feminine; singular/plural endings vary by adjective.
mistakes: ❌ une homme heureux → une femme heureuse

French.rule: French normally requires an explicit subject pronoun with a finite verb.
French.formation: je, tu, il/elle/on, nous, vous, ils/elles.
mistakes: ❌ Travaille aujourd'hui. → Usually: Je travaille aujourd'hui.

French.rule: Possessive adjectives agree with the possessed noun and number, not with the owner.
French.formation: mon/ma/mes; ton/ta/tes; son/sa/ses; notre/nos; votre/vos; leur/leurs.
mistakes: ❌ mon maison → ✅ ma maison

French.rule: French questions can use intonation, est-ce que or inversion.
French.formation: Tu viens ? / Est-ce que tu viens ? / Viens-tu ?
mistakes: ❌ Est-ce que viens-tu ? → Don't combine forms unnecessarily.

French.rule: Basic negation places ne before the conjugated verb and pas after it.
French.formation: ne + verb + pas; ne becomes n' before vowel sound.
mistakes: ❌ Je pas parle → ✅ Je ne parle pas

French.rule: C'est commonly introduces or identifies a noun; il/elle est commonly precedes an adjective or profession without an article.
French.formation: c'est + noun; il/elle est + adjective/profession in common patterns.
mistakes: ❌ C'est gentil? Context matters; use il est gentil for a person.

French.rule: Use à, dans, sur, sous, devant, derrière, entre and related expressions for location.
French.formation: à/dans/sur + place; country prepositions require gender/number patterns.
examples: Le livre est sur la table.
mistakes: ❌ sur la maison when meaning inside → dans la maison

French.rule: French uses expressions such as à for clock time, en for months/years and le for recurring days.
French.formation: à 8h; en juillet; le lundi; pendant deux heures.
mistakes: ❌ en lundi → recurring day: le lundi

French.rule: Passé composé commonly uses avoir or être + past participle.
French.formation: avoir/être in present + participe passé.
mistakes: ❌ J'ai allé → Aller uses être: je suis allé.

French.rule: Imparfait describes background, habits and ongoing states in the past.
French.formation: nous present stem + ais, ais, ait, ions, iez, aient; être → ét-.
examples: Quand j'étais jeune, je lisais beaucoup.
mistakes: ❌ Single completed event usually needs passé composé.

French.rule: Use passé composé for completed events and imparfait for background or habitual context.
French.formation: event = passé composé; background = imparfait.
examples: Il pleuvait quand je suis arrivé.
Je lisais quand il a téléphoné.
mistakes: ❌ Don't use one tense for every past verb.

French.rule: Aller + infinitive expresses a near or planned future.
French.formation: vais/vas/va/allons/allez/vont + infinitive.
mistakes: ❌ Je vais partir, not je vais à partir.

French.rule: The future is formed with the infinitive (or irregular stem) plus future endings.
French.formation: -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont.
mistakes: ❌ je travaillerais when simple future is intended.

French.rule: Pouvoir, devoir and vouloir express ability/permission, obligation and desire.
French.formation: pouvoir/devoir/vouloir + infinitive.
French.hook: CAN → POUVOIR • MUST → DEVOIR • WANT → VOULOIR
mistakes: ❌ Je peux à venir → modal + infinitive directly.

French.rule: Use plus, moins and aussi with que to compare adjectives, adverbs or nouns.
French.formation: plus/moins/aussi + adjective + que; mieux/meilleur special forms.
examples: Paul est plus grand que Marc.
mistakes: ❌ plus meilleur → meilleur already means better.

French.rule: Direct and indirect object pronouns replace nouns and normally appear before the verb.
French.formation: me, te, le/la, lui, nous, vous, les, leur.
mistakes: ❌ Je vois le → ✅ Je le vois.

French.rule: Y can replace certain places or à + thing; en can replace de + thing or quantities.
French.formation: y → place/à; en → de/quantity.
French.hook: Y = THERE • EN = OF IT / SOME
mistakes: ❌ J'y parle de lui in the wrong context; choose according to the preposition.
questions: Tu vas à Paris ? Oui, j'___ vais.

French.rule: Qui, que, dont and où connect a noun to a relative clause.
French.formation: qui = subject; que = object; dont = de; où = place/time.
French.hook: QUI DOES • QUE RECEIVES • DONT = DE
examples: La femme qui parle est ma sœur.
Le livre que je lis est intéressant.
La ville où je vis est calme.
mistakes: ❌ La femme que parle → qui is subject.
questions: Le livre ___ je lis est bon.

French.rule: French uses present + future/imperative for real conditions and imperfect + conditional for hypothetical ones.
French.formation: si + present → future; si + imperfect → conditional.
examples: Si tu viens, je serai content.
Si j'avais le temps, je voyagerais.
mistakes: ❌ Si j'aurais le temps → Si j'avais le temps.

French.rule: The imperative gives commands, advice and instructions.
French.formation: tu/vous/nous forms; pronoun placement changes in affirmative commands.
mistakes: ❌ Tu écoute ! → Imperative: Écoute !

French.rule: The subjunctive often follows necessity, emotion, doubt, desire and certain conjunctions.
French.formation: que + subjunctive after trigger.
mistakes: ❌ Il faut que tu viens → viennes.

French.rule: French passive voice uses être + past participle, with agreement.
French.formation: être + participe passé; tense is carried by être.
examples: Le bâtiment a été construit en 1900.
mistakes: ❌ La lettre est envoyé → feminine agreement: envoyée.

French.rule: Reported speech introduces what someone said with que, si or question words and may require tense changes.
French.formation: il a dit que...; il a demandé si...
examples: Il a dit qu'il était fatigué.
Elle a demandé si je venais.
mistakes: ❌ Il a dit moi → Il m'a dit / Il a dit que...

French.rule: Plus-que-parfait expresses an action completed before another past action.
French.formation: imparfait of avoir/être + past participle.
examples: J'avais déjà mangé quand il est arrivé.
mistakes: ❌ J'ai déjà mangé quand il est arrivé can change the sequence meaning.
questions: J'___ déjà mangé quand il est arrivé.

French.rule: Connectors such as pourtant, cependant, puisque, tandis que, bien que and afin que express precise logical relations.
French.formation: connector + appropriate clause; subjunctive after certain triggers.
examples: Bien qu'il soit tard, nous continuons.
mistakes: ❌ Bien que + indicative in standard formal usage → often subjunctive.
